body: RAG and durable process memory (decision ledgers, ADRs, correction history) are needed across all platform editions, but community/local editions require zero-external-dependency storage while enterprise/SaaS requires scalable pgvector. This adapter provides a unified interface across all editions.
_note: Full authoring of context, epic, and ACs

brief.problem: Knowledge item indexing, architectural memory, and code search require vector storage that operates both embedded locally (SQLite-vss) and scalable in enterprise clusters (PostgreSQL pgvector).
brief.what_adds: Dual-Engine RAG and Memory Storage Adapter with automatic backend detection and hybrid semantic/lexical search.

label: PF Backlog 687
risks: SQLite-vss platform compilation compatibility on Windows mitigated via pre-built extension binaries.
title: Dual-Engine RAG and Memory Storage Adapter: embedded SQLite-vss for local editions and PostgreSQL pgvector for enterprise
summary: Implement a dual-engine storage adapter interface for vector and lexical retrieval that transparently switches between embedded SQLite-vss (local) and PostgreSQL/pgvector (enterprise).

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing components/APIs: core/agent_memory.py, core/generator_adapters.py, core/intake_adapters.py, core/memory_api.py

approach: Create VectorStoreProtocol with SqliteVssBackend and PgVectorBackend implementations selected via database DSN connection string.
rollback: Revert to lexical BM25 search fallback in core/search.py.
objective: Build a pluggable dual-engine vector adapter supporting embedded SQLite-vss for community/local editions and pgvector for enterprise SaaS clusters.
verification: Contract tests verifying embedding insertion, nearest neighbor retrieval, and cross-engine query equivalence.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Vector storage adapter abstracts embedding indexing and cosine similarity queries across SQLite-vss and PostgreSQL pgvector backends.
AC-2: Community edition runs zero-dependency local vector store using sqlite-vss without requiring external daemon infrastructure.
AC-3: Enterprise edition seamlessly switches to PostgreSQL pgvector with tenant isolation and row-level security enforcement.
